researched.name: Wendt (India) Ltd
researched.reason: The trigger is real - Q2 FY27 consolidated sales Rs 71.98 cr (+28%) and PAT Rs 5.49 cr (+103%), H1 sales Rs 142.91 cr (+33%) and PAT Rs 11.67 cr (+80%), zero debt, Murugappa group. It does not clear the bar once the ten-year record in the FY26 annual report is read. Standalone net sales went Rs 127.79 cr (FY17) to Rs 206.52 cr (FY26) - a 4.9% compound rate over nine years. Consolidated PAT went Rs 40.09 cr (FY23), Rs 40.95 cr (FY24), Rs 39.48 cr (FY25), Rs 14.55 cr (FY26): the 'growth' now being reported is a recovery off a 63% collapse, and H1 FY27 annualised is still well under the FY24 level. Against that, BSE's header shows PE 53.51 on trailing standalone EPS of Rs 137.70. Also read and weighed: Wendt GmbH (since renamed PG&F Super Abrasives GmbH) divested its ENTIRE 37.50% stake in May 2025, so CUMI alone is now the 37.5% promoter and the public holds 62.5%; the Executive Director and CEO post has been vacant past the three-month statutory window (the board was still searching at the date of the FY26 report) and the exchange levied a fine on which the board commented on 03-Mar-2026; the auditor records that the accounting software's audit trail was not maintained at the application level; and the exchanges have twice asked the company to clarify volume movement (15-Jun and 11-Sep-2026). A good company at a price that pays for growth it has not delivered in a decade.

researched.name: Millworks Technologies Ltd
researched.reason: Today's trigger carries no number: two DEVELOPMENTAL purchase orders from HAL (oxygen valve assemblies for the HAWK via the Overhaul Division, surge warning sensor assemblies for the MiG-29's RD-33 via the Engine Division, Koraput) and an MoU with TridenTech Engineering of IIT Madras Research Park for co-developing a UAV internal-combustion engine on a revenue-share basis. No value, no quantity, no timeline is stated for any of the three. The other 'DEAL' signal turned out on reading to be LRSD Capital SELLING 20,000 shares (3.44% -> 3.32%), not an acquisition. Then the FY26 audited accounts, which are the reason this is a firm no: revenue Rs 148.77 cr (from Rs 22.00 cr in FY25, +576%) with trade receivables of Rs 138.69 cr at 31-Mar-2026 - 340 days of sales - of which Rs 76.02 cr is over six months old and the provision for doubtful debts is NIL; receivables consumed Rs 123.37 cr of cash in the year, leaving cash generated from operations at Rs 0.44 cr and net cash from operations NEGATIVE after Rs 2.07 cr of taxes paid. The CARO report states that undisputed statutory dues including provident fund, ESI and income tax 'have not been regularly deposited during the year', tabulates repayment delays of 1 to 30 days across SIDBI, UGRO, Clix and Protium facilities, and the balance sheet carries Rs 68.94 lakh of interest payable on MSME creditors (Rs 5.05 lakh the year before). The company has filed NO quarterly or half-yearly results since listing on 21-Jul-2026, and the market capitalisation of Rs 1,764.5 cr is about 48x FY26 PAT at roughly 3x the IPO price. Not an idea at any price until a cash-collecting half-year is on file.

data_problems: SCORECARD DEFECT, FOUND THIS RUN - the Bhagyanagar India return on this page is not a measured return. track.json shows the card at +50.7% (Rs 40.45 -> Rs 60.95) with the adjustment event '2026-10-08 x11 unrecorded gap x10.96'. The event on that date is not a bonus or a split: BSE filing 7b3ee1ae of 25-Sep-2026 records the NCLT-sanctioned Composite Scheme of Arrangement under which ONE share of Tieramet Limited (FV Rs 2) is issued for every ONE share held in Bhagyanagar India, record date Thursday 08-October-2026. A demerger cannot be expressed as a single multiplicative factor - the holder keeps the parent share AND receives the resulting-company share, so the true return needs both legs, and Tieramet has not been seen trading in any source read in this run. The +50.7% should be read as unmeasured. An update saying so has been written onto the card. scripts/ideas/*.py were NOT touched (the routine forbids it); this is flagged for the owner, since score.py's inferred-gap logic will keep producing this number on every future run until a demerger is handled separately from a split.
